beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process repeatedly updates windowed features with shared parameters.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image field from the compact recurrent computation that updates it. The encoder first converts the low-resolution image into features. Windowing groups those features without leaving the dense carrier behind. The DQ-CTM thought process runs for repeated ticks with shared parameters. The recurrence returns to the thought process itself, so each tick refines the same stage. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier through shared DQ-CTM ticks
params.note: The loop stays inside the thought stage, not around the full flow.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features from the low-resolution image, then window partitioning produces tokens while preserving the feature field.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The equation defines the dense carrier before the recurrent thought process touches it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition acts on that full feature field, so the tokens come from the dense carrier.

params.headline: The carrier is encoded first, then partitioned into windows

terms.label: encoder turns the low-resolution image into dense features
window partition keeps every token from the feature field
